pharm: Binds cereblon (E3 ubiquitin ligase) - degrades Ikaros/Aiolos; immunomodulatory, antiangiogenic, antineoplastic
tags: BOXED WARNING: embryo-fetal toxicity AND venous/arterial thromboembolism
quick: Multiple myeloma: 4 mg PO once daily on Days 1-21 of 28-day cycles (with dexamethasone); Kaposi sarcoma: 5 mg/day Days 1-21
Take with or without food; swallow capsule whole at about the same time daily
CONTRAINDICATED - teratogen; 2 negative tests before start, contraception during + 4 weeks after
Discontinue breastfeeding - potential serious harm to infant
Severe (eGFR <30) not on dialysis: 3 mg/day; on haemodialysis: 2 mg/day after dialysis
CBC weekly first 8 weeks then monthly, pregnancy tests, signs of VTE/ATE, infection, neuropathy, LFTs
summary: Pomalidomide is an oral thalidomide-analogue immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) used, with dexamethasone, for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after at least two prior therapies (including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor) and for AIDS-related or HIV-negative Kaposi sarcoma. The myeloma dose is 4 mg once daily on Days 1-21 of repeated 28-day cycles; Kaposi sarcoma uses 5 mg/day on the same schedule. It carries a BOXED WARNING for embryo-fetal toxicity (a thalidomide analogue and known human teratogen) and for venous and arterial thromboembolism, and is available only through the restricted Pomalyst REMS programme. Two negative pregnancy tests and two forms of contraception are mandatory in females of reproductive potential. Major toxicities include myelosuppression, thromboembolism, infection, and second primary malignancies.
indications: Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (with dexamethasone) after at least 2 prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, with progression on/within 60 days of the last therapy
AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma after failure of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART)

dosage.d: 4 mg once daily on Days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle
dosage.t: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; dexamethasone per regimen
dosage.n: Modify for haematologic and other toxicities

dosage.d: 5 mg once daily on Days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle
dosage.t: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: 2 mg once daily, taken after the haemodialysis session on dialysis days

admin: Swallow capsules whole with water; do not break, chew, or open
Take at about the same time each day, with or without food
Handle capsules minimally; if powder contacts skin/mucosa, wash thoroughly (cytotoxic/teratogenic)
Dispense and obtain only through the Pomalyst REMS programme
Confirm two negative pregnancy tests in females of reproductive potential before the first dose
Consider thromboprophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulant) based on VTE risk
moa: Pomalidomide is a thalidomide analogue with immunomodulatory, antiangiogenic, and antineoplastic properties. Its activities are mediated through binding to cereblon, the substrate-recognition component of a cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. This redirects the ligase to ubiquitinate the transcription factors Aiolos and Ikaros, targeting them for proteasomal degradation - producing direct cytotoxic and immunomodulatory effects, including inhibition of malignant B-cell/plasma-cell proliferation, induction of apoptosis (including in lenalidomide-resistant myeloma cells), T-cell and NK-cell activation, and inhibition of angiogenesis.

absolute: Pregnancy (teratogenic thalidomide analogue - causes severe birth defects or embryo-fetal death)
Severe hypersensitivity (e.g. angioedema, anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous reactions) to pomalidomide
relative: History of venous or arterial thromboembolism (VTE/ATE risk - use thromboprophylaxis)
Hepatic impairment (smoking induces CYP1A2 and lowers exposure)
Concomitant strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin)
monitor: Signs/symptoms of VTE/PE and arterial events (MI, stroke)

preg: BOXED WARNING / CONTRAINDICATED. Pomalidomide is a thalidomide analogue and a known human teratogen causing severe, life-threatening birth defects or embryo-fetal death. Females of reproductive potential must have two negative pregnancy tests before starting, use two reliable forms of contraception (or continuous abstinence) beginning 4 weeks before, during, during dose interruptions, and for 4 weeks after the last dose, and undergo regular pregnancy testing. Males (including vasectomised) must use a condom during and for 4 weeks after the last dose and must not donate sperm. Distribution is only through the Pomalyst REMS programme.
lact: It is not known whether pomalidomide is excreted in human milk, but it is present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for some time after the last dose.
renal: For severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) not requiring dialysis, reduce the dose to 3 mg once daily. For patients requiring haemodialysis, give 2 mg once daily, administered after the haemodialysis session on dialysis days. No dose adjustment is needed for mild-to-moderate impairment.
hepatic: For mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A or B), reduce the starting dose to 3 mg once daily. For severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C), reduce to 2 mg once daily. Monitor hepatic function.

major: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors e.g. fluvoxamine (avoid; if combined with a strong P-gp inhibitor too, reduce pomalidomide dose by 50%)
Other thromboembolism-promoting agents (erythropoietins, hormone therapy) - increased VTE risk
Dexamethasone and other immunosuppressants (additive infection/VTE risk)
moderate: Strong CYP1A2 inducers and cigarette smoking (induce CYP1A2, reducing pomalidomide exposure/efficacy)
interactions.food: No clinically significant food effect; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid or limit - additive fatigue, dizziness, and somnolence
interactions.diagnostics: Pregnancy testing is mandatory; monitor CBC and LFTs - cytopenias and transaminase elevations are common

serious: Severe neutropenia / febrile neutropenia and serious infections (including sepsis, pneumonia)
Second primary malignancies (AML, MDS, solid tumours)
rare: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (rare reports with immunomodulators)
emergency: Acute thromboembolic event - MI, stroke, massive PE
Tumour lysis syndrome with metabolic derangement

monitoring: Pregnancy tests per REMS schedule in females of reproductive potential
Complete blood count weekly for the first 8 weeks, then monthly (neutropenia/thrombocytopenia)
Signs and symptoms of thromboembolism (VTE and arterial)
Electrolytes/uric acid if high tumour burden (tumour lysis)
counsel: This drug can cause severe birth defects or fetal death - it must never be taken during pregnancy
Use two reliable methods of contraception (women) and always a condom (men) per the REMS programme
Do not donate blood while taking it or for 4 weeks after, and men must not donate sperm
Report leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, or sudden weakness/speech difficulty at once (clot/stroke)
Report fever or signs of infection promptly - your blood counts can fall
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or severe rash
Swallow capsules whole; do not open or crush; wash skin if it contacts the powder
You can only get this medicine through the special REMS pharmacy programme
pk: Antineoplastic effect assessed over treatment cycles; absorbed with Tmax ~2-3 h
Plasma Cmax approximately 2 to 3 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 7.5 hours (about 9.5 hours in multiple myeloma patients)
Once-daily dosing on Days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle
Store at 20-25 degrees C (excursions 15-30 degrees C); keep in original container
pearls: BOXED WARNING (dual): embryo-fetal toxicity (thalidomide analogue) AND venous/arterial thromboembolism.
Available only through the restricted Pomalyst REMS programme - two negative pregnancy tests before start, two contraception methods during and for 4 weeks after.
Thromboprophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulation) is recommended given the VTE/ATE risk.
Cigarette smoking induces CYP1A2 and lowers pomalidomide exposure; strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine) raise it - reduce dose 50% if combined with a strong 1A2 + P-gp inhibitor.
Monitor CBC weekly for the first 8 weeks; dose-modify for neutropenia/thrombocytopenia.
Watch for second primary malignancies and rare hepatotoxicity/severe skin reactions.
missed: If a dose is missed and it is less than 12 hours since the scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the usual time the following day. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose may intensify haematologic toxicity (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) and other adverse effects. Manage with supportive care: monitor blood counts, treat cytopenias and infection (growth factors, transfusion, antibiotics as needed), and provide symptomatic measures. Pomalidomide is dialysable - haemodialysis may be considered to enhance removal.
